title: Prime Nim losing positions are not automatic
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: In Prime Nim you remove a prime number of stones; the player who cannot move loses. Show that no finite automaton reading pile sizes in any base can recognise the losing positions.
math: Let $L\subseteq\mathbb N$ be defined recursively by $n\in L\iff n-p\notin L$ for every prime $p\le n$ (the P-positions of the subtraction game with subtraction set the primes; $L=\{0,1,9,10,25,34,35,49,\dots\}$, OEIS A025043). Prove that for no integer $k\ge2$ is the characteristic sequence of $L$ $k$-automatic.
